newsitem.title: USA: Vitro 's Anchor intends to sell assets.
newsitem.headline: Vitro 's Anchor intends to sell assets.

text.p: Vitro SA said Friday its Anchor Glass Container Corp subsidiary signed a tentative agreement to sell its assets to Ball-Foster Glass Container Co.

To assure its continued operations until the sale, Anchor's board of directors voluntarily filed a petition for protection under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, as reported earlier in the afternoon, Vitro said in a statement.
Vitro also said it would no longer support Anchor's liquidity needs.
The glass container company had said in August it would solicit offers for Anchor, given slowing U.S. glass container demand and Anchor's unfavorable operating results and continuing liquidity needs.
Vitro and Anchor conducted intensive negotiations with prospective buyers over the past few weeks, Vitro said.
Ball-Foster is 42 percent owned by Indiana-based container company Ball Corp and 58 percent owned by French glass container company Compagnie de Saint-Gobain.
Vitro would not comment further on the deal.
Tampa, Fla.-based Anchor Glass, the third-largest company in the U.S. glass container industry, also refused to comment on the deal and Ball-Foster was not immediately available.
A hight-ranking Vitro official said last week Vitro hoped to use proceeds from the sale to reduce its debt load and focus on more profitable core businesses in Mexico and elsewhere.
